problem: The frozen minimum-information language contains two distinct counts: at least 100 otherwise eligible first-breeding events, and at least 50 events with at least two observed candidate colonies. The first choice-engine implementation only receives multi-candidate choice rows and therefore incorrectly used the same model-event count for both thresholds, effectively requiring >=100 multi-candidate events.

source_gate.definition: Known-age first-breeding events satisfying the frozen state, temporal, performance, colony-size and detection-availability rules before requiring a candidate set of at least two actually visited colonies.

choice_model_gate.definition: Subset of source-gate events whose two-season PB candidate set contains 2-3 Ross colonies and includes the first breeding colony.

implementation_change: The parser/state-builder must produce an outcome-blind source-gate receipt containing the count of eligible first-breeding events before the multi-candidate filter.
The conditional-choice engine accepts that source count explicitly.
The engine requires source_count >=100 and model_choice_events >=50, rather than requiring model_choice_events >=100.
All biological eligibility rules, covariates, candidate-set rules, permutation inference and alpha remain unchanged.
why_not_posthoc_relaxation: No real Ross behavioral row, first-breeding event count, candidate-set size, destination, coefficient or p-value has been inspected. This change restores the literal two-stage thresholds already written in the original frozen gate rather than choosing a threshold in response to observed sample size.
claim_boundary: Do not lower either 100 or 50 after data access.
Do not count events excluded by the frozen detection, performance, size, state or temporal rules toward the source gate.
Do not count a one-colony prospecting history as a choice-model event.
If source gate passes but choice-model gate fails, stop without fitting the performance-choice coefficient.
